intro: Follow how a text links ideas and how later phrases refer back to earlier information.
b1.titulo: Follow the thread of the text
b1.texto: Connectors show relations between ideas: **porque** gives a reason, **por ello** introduces a result and **a pesar de** marks a concession. A noun phrase such as **esa iniciativa** can refer to an idea mentioned earlier. To understand a paragraph, ask both how its sentences connect and what each reference points to.
b2.f0: Last year, several residents turned an empty plot into a community garden.
b2.f1: The initiative began with six families, but now two neighbourhood schools also take part.
b2.f2: Although the space is small, the people who look after it have planted herbs, tomatoes and flowers for insects.
b2.f3: For that reason, the group has asked the council for a water tap and a cupboard for tools.
b2.f4: That request has not yet been approved. Meanwhile, participants bring water from home and organise maintenance shifts.
b2.f5: In addition, one of the schools holds science workshops in the garden and takes its classes there once a month.
b2.f6: The organisers hope that this collaboration will continue through the summer, although they have not yet decided who will water the plants.
b2.f7: The project does not produce enough food for the whole neighbourhood; even so, its organisers think it is worthwhile because of the activities and participation it creates.
b4.o0.refuerzo: Esa petición points back to the request for the tap and the cupboard, the noun just mentioned.
b4.o1.refuerzo: Planting tomatoes is not what petición refers to; it points back to the request.
b4.o2.refuerzo: The empty plot is mentioned, but esa petición points to the request itself.
b5.o0.refuerzo: Por ello means for this reason, so it introduces a result of the information before.
b5.o1.refuerzo: Por ello introduces a result, not a contrast; a contrast would use pero or sin embargo.
b5.o2.refuerzo: Por ello is not a time sequence; it links a result to the previous information.
b6.pregunta: Which limitation of the project is stated?
b6.o0.refuerzo: The text states that the project does not produce enough food for the whole neighbourhood.
b6.o1.refuerzo: Having no school participants is not the limitation; the stated limit is the amount of food.
b6.o2.refuerzo: Being approved for expansion is a positive status, not a limitation of the project.
b7.o0.refuerzo: A pesar de means despite; it introduces a fact that does not stop people from joining.
b7.o1.refuerzo: Por ello means for this reason, a result; the sentence needs a concession, despite.
b7.o2.refuerzo: Porque means because, a cause; the sentence needs a concession, like despite.
b8.o1: Afterwards, the participants cancelled the shifts.
b8.o1.explicacion: Check the meaning of the Spanish sentence.
b8.o2: For that reason, the participants leave the project.
b8.o2.explicacion: Check the meaning of the Spanish sentence.
b9.traduccion: Although it is small, the garden brings many people together.
b8.o0.explicacion: Mientras tanto means meanwhile, linking the sentence to the time.
